title: Bulgarian Split Squat
summary: A one-leg squat with your rear foot up on a bench, for the quads and glutes.

muscles.why: Library rating 1 for quads (main mover): each working set adds 1 of a set to the weekly quads total.
Library rating 0.8 for glutes (main mover): each working set adds 0.8 of a set to the weekly glutes total.
Library rating 0.5 for adductors (helper): each working set adds 0.5 of a set to the weekly adductors total.
Library rating 0.5 for abductors (helper): each working set adds 0.5 of a set to the weekly abductors total.

setup.text: Stand in front of a bench with the top of your rear foot resting on it.
Lower straight down until your rear knee nearly touches the floor.
Keep your front foot flat and your knee tracking over your toes.
Drive up through your front foot.

form_cues.cue: Drop the back knee straight down
Drive up through the front heel
A longer stride and leaning forward work the glutes more. A shorter stride and staying upright work the quads more.

mistakes.text: Standing too close to the bench so the front heel lifts.

lower_risk.text: Warm-up: the app adds up to 2 ramp-up sets only when the load is heavy for the equipment and the main muscle is not warm yet.
The app suggests a heavier load only when the jump is 7.5% or less; otherwise it adds a rep first.
Default target: 8-12 reps, stopping about 3 reps short of failure (RIR 3). Stop the set when form breaks down.
Use the same controlled range on every rep; lower under control rather than dropping or bouncing.
Pick a variation and range you can train comfortably.
